questions.q: What does tokenizing a piece of text do?
options: Encrypts the text so it can be stored safely
Translates the text into a different language
Splits the cleaned string into units, usually words, that can be counted
Removes every word that appears more than once
questions.explain: Tokenization splits a string into units (usually words) so that a model can count or otherwise represent them.

questions.q: In the lesson, the review 'Not a good battery' became ['good', 'battery'] after stop-word removal. Why is that a problem?
options: The word 'battery' should have been removed too
The default stop-word list contains 'not', so the negation is deleted and the meaning flips
Stop-word removal always makes the vocabulary larger
The tokens are in the wrong order
questions.explain: scikit-learn's English stop list includes 'not'. Removing it turns a negative statement into a positive-looking one, which is dangerous for sentiment tasks.

questions.q: Which statement about stemming is accurate?
options: Stemmers use a dictionary and always return real words
Stemming is required before any text can be modeled
A stemmer can never change the meaning of a token
Stemming rules chop suffixes, so the output can be a non-word such as 'batterie'
questions.explain: Stemmers apply suffix-chopping rules. That is fast, but stems like 'lov' or 'batterie' are not real words. Lemmatizers use dictionaries to return real base forms.

questions.q: The lesson's cleaning regex kept only letters and apostrophes, so the digit in 'lasts 2 days' was dropped. What is the right takeaway?
options: Cleaning rules should be chosen for your data and task; keep digits if they matter, such as error codes
Digits are never useful in text and should always be removed
Regular expressions cannot match digits
Digits are removed automatically by every tokenizer
questions.explain: Every cleaning rule discards information. Decide per task; for support tickets containing error codes, digits may be exactly what you need.

questions.q: Which is the best description of the text pipeline in this lesson?
options: Train, validate, test, deploy
Tokenize, then always remove every word shorter than five letters
Normalize, tokenize, filter, reduce, where each step is an optional decision about what to discard
Lowercase, then translate, then encrypt
questions.explain: The pipeline is normalize, tokenize, optionally filter stop words, optionally reduce to a root form, choosing each step deliberately.
